Subject: Junction AI onboarding — model shortlist, context length & hourly token bands

Hi Ava / Liam —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. To keep the implementation sprint tight, can you confirm two things so we can map models and capacity: 

1) Typical context needs per request (average and 95th percentile) — e.g., average prompt tokens, average completion tokens, and 95th percentile end-to-end token length.
2) Hourly inbound request distribution (sample for peak and off-peak hours) and any expected burst windows (start/end times).

If you have a small sample export, drop it as a CSV — a single day with timestamps and prompt+response token counts is ideal. I attached a small template (junction_sample_traffic.csv) you can use.

Our aim after we get this is: produce a 3-model shortlist tuned for cost/latency (low/medium/high context), and an hourly token-band projection with recommended routing (hosted vs dedicated) and caching suggestions.

Target timeline: receipt of data by EOD Wed (Apr 14) so Monica and I can publish the shortlist and cost bands by Apr 16 for your internal review.

Thanks —
Ben

Hi Ben —

Thanks — attaching the export you asked for and a short doc with example prompts. Quick notes up front:
- Average prompt tokens: 72
- Average completion tokens: 180
- 95th percentile total tokens: ~820 (we have long transcripts for some accounts)
- Typical hourly distribution: baseline ~220 req/hr, peak windows (region-specific) up to 3,200 req/hr for 30–90 min; predictable daily peaks around 10:00–11:00 PDT and 14:00–15:00 PDT.

See attached: junction_sample_traffic.csv (one-week anonymized sample) and example_prompts_and_responses.pdf. We flagged three customer tiers in the CSV: sandbox, standard, enterprise. The enterprise tier drives the 95th pct spikes.

Let us know if you want additional segmentation (by user cohort or feature flag).

Best,
Ava

From: monica_patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Junction AI onboarding — model shortlist, context length & hourly token bands

Nice dataset — thanks Ava. Quick internal read and proposed approach: 

- Data summary (quick): mean total tokens ~252, median ~210, 95th ~820; hourly median requests ~200, peak short bursts up to 3.2k.
- Risk vector: spikes driven by enterprise batch exports / long transcripts; caching will help for repeated prefixes on standard tier users but not for long transcript completions.

Model shortlist proposal (three tracks):
1) Latency-cost baseline: Mistral-7B-int8 or similar — good for standard tier (avg tokens) with low cost.
2) Balanced quality: Llama-2-13B-8bit / Red-13B-q4 — for standard+enterprise where quality matters and latency SLO is ~300–600ms.
3) High-quality long-context: Redwood-Long-34B-16k or a 33B LLM with extended context + KV cache strategy for enterprise transcript completions.

Sizing & routing recommendations (preliminary):
- Baseline routing: standard (sandbox/standard) -> hosted API on low-cost pool; enterprise -> dedicated capacity with long-context runner.
- Autoscale policy: allow burst capacity for enterprise pools with warm-start windows at expected daily peaks; pre-warm 10 min before 10:00 and 14:00 PDT.
- Hourly token bands: we should produce (a) median/hr, (b) 95th/hr, (c) peak-15min window tokens. I'll sketch tables once Ben confirms scope.

Ben — can you confirm the timeline? I can have a draft shortlist + hourly bands by Apr 16 if we treat the sample as representative. If Junction wants cohort breakdowns, add one day.

Cheers,
Monica

--
